clue.text: Detective in Poe's house not starting with 20,perhaps

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter of the word for Poe's house is dropped

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote The Fall of the House of Usher
the answer to 20 is Yale, a make of lock

explanation.surface: A sleuth is found at the home of Edgar Allan Poe, linked somehow to clue 20.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' cuts the U from USHER, leaving SHER. The cross-reference names YALE, which is to be read as an example of a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes is the most famous fictional sleuth, known by his first name alone.

clue.text: Second glutton to turn tap

parts.note: a pig is a greedy eater

indicators.note: turn means the little word to is turned round

explanation.surface: Another greedy eater goes to switch on the faucet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like turning a tap but reverses TO to OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A valve or faucet controlling the flow from a barrel.

clue.text: Corrupt senate gets at people of property

indicators.note: corrupt means the letters of senate gets at are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A crooked senate attacks the landed classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets at' reads as 'attacks' but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Realtors deal in houses; whimsically, people concerned with property.

clue.text: Bass in audition who provided notes for 5

indicators.note: in audition says the word for bass is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a bass voice or note is low

explanation.surface: A bass singer at a tryout, the one who composed tunes for another clue's lyricist.
explanation.walkthrough: Frederick Loewe composed the music for Lerner's lyrics; his name is said like LOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Loewe was the composer partner of the lyricist Lerner, writing the music for their shows.

clue.text: Stonemason at work may be brisk and cheerful

explanation.surface: A working stonemason might be lively and upbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: A stonemason at work chips at stone, so is a chipper.
explanation.definitionFit: One who chips stone; also an informal adjective for lively and in good spirits.

clue.text: Student in audition who provided words for 3

indicators.note: in audition says the word for student is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a student is a learner

explanation.surface: A pupil turns up at a tryout, the one who wrote lyrics for another clue's composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Jay Lerner wrote the lyrics for Frederick Loewe's music (My Fair Lady); LEARNER and LERNER are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Lerner was the lyricist partner of the composer Loewe, so he supplied the words to Loewe's tunes.

clue.text: They may bring about exit with cross!

definitions.text: They may bring about exit with cross!

indicators.note: bring about means the letters of exit and cross are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Priests drive out demons with a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: those who expel spirits do so brandishing a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Priests who expel evil spirits, often wielding a crucifix, cause the demon's departure.

clue.text: Tarzan climbing — right for title role

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: Tarzan is the ape man of the jungle

explanation.surface: Tarzan scales a tree and is the right choice for the starring part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' fits Tarzan in the trees but turns APEMAN upward to NAMEPA.
explanation.definitionFit: The character a play or film is named after, the eponymous lead.

clue.text: Call on team for seats near arena

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Phone the squad about places close to the action.
explanation.definitionFit: The front rows beside a boxing ring are the closest places to watch from.

clue.text: Daring Pinter play I would put on

indicators.note: put on means the following piece is attached after the first
play means the letters of the playwright's name are rearranged, playing with them

parts.note: I would contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A bold Harold Pinter drama gets staged by me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a noun about Pinter's drama but shuffles PINTER into INTREP; 'put on' adds ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A daring person is fearless, the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Author and dispatcher of French letters?

explanation.surface: A writer is also the one who posts condoms.
explanation.walkthrough: French letters is British slang for condoms; read literally, a Norman (French) mailer sends letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Mailer was an American novelist; whimsically, a Norman is French and a mailer sends letters.

clue.text: Horses scatter over surface

explanation.surface: Horses spread across the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeding establishment for horses; also a verb meaning dot or strew across something.

clue.text: Photo sent out then and there

indicators.note: out signals the letters of photo sent are put out of order

explanation.surface: A picture has been dispatched straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something immediately, at the very place and moment, is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Heads and shoulders may be covered by them

definitions.text: Heads and shoulders may be covered by them

parts.words: Heads and shoulders may be covered by them
parts.note: headlands are heads, and sleeveless cloaks cover the shoulders, so the clue works as a garment and as coastal landforms

explanation.surface: Something that covers the head and shoulders, like a hood or shampoo.
explanation.walkthrough: Heads and Shoulders suggests the shampoo; a cape is both a cloak over the shoulders and a headland, a 'head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloaks drape over the shoulders, while headlands are also called heads along a coastline.

clue.text: 6 deliveries completed

explanation.surface: Six bowls have been finished.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a set of six balls bowled from one end is called an over.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket term for six balls bowled in sequence; also an adjective meaning finished or ended.

clue.text: Material for former GI in 11 parts?

indicators.note: in says the old soldier goes inside the other letters
parts means the number written out is broken into pieces and rearranged

parts.note: the number written in words
a vet is a veteran, a former soldier

explanation.surface: Cloth meant for an old soldier comes in eleven pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a cross-reference to STUD but is the bare number; 'parts' shuffles its spelling into VELEEN, and 'in' puts the old soldier inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotton fabric with a short pile imitating velvet.

clue.text: Wanted to be made fatherless?

explanation.surface: Someone longed to lose a father.
explanation.walkthrough: A sire is a father, so being de-sired would humorously mean losing one.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanted means longed for; also a jokey coinage of removing a sire, a father.

clue.text: Possibly name in memoirs needing correction?

definitions.text: Possibly name in memoirs needing correction?

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for name goes inside memoirs
needing correction means the letters must be put right, rearranged

explanation.surface: A name in an autobiography may be wrong and want fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a wrongly applied name in memoirs needs correcting.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong or inappropriate label is exactly a name needing to be corrected.

clue.text: Fine print is attractive

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an etching is a print from an etched plate

explanation.surface: A fine engraving is good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A charming or appealing look, as in a fetching hat.

clue.text: In a perfect world I do business and play, ignoring the odds

parts.note: to deal is to trade or do business

indicators.note: ignoring the odds means only the even-placed letters of play are kept

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of running a company and having fun, without worrying about the chances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring the odds' sounds like recklessness but drops the 1st and 3rd letters of PLAY, leaving LY.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning under the best possible circumstances.

clue.text: Drink provided by US hostel or university

indicators.note: provided by means the drink comes after the hostel

parts.note: the Y is the American name for the YMCA, a hostel
ale is beer, a drink

explanation.surface: Beer is supplied by an American hostel or college.
explanation.walkthrough: In America the YMCA, a cheap hostel, is called 'the Y'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ivy League institution in New Haven, Connecticut.

clue.text: A number of Romans like hot potatoes

parts.note: a Roman numeral, M being a thousand
like means as
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Many Romans enjoy hot spuds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number of Romans' suggests a crowd, but means one Roman numeral, M.
explanation.definitionFit: Mash is the British word for mashed spuds, as in bangers and mash.

clue.text: Souvenir is same in France, not different

parts.note: meme is French for same

indicators.note: different means the letters of not are made different, rearranged

explanation.surface: A keepsake is the same in France, not changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not different' reads as 'identical' but 'different' shuffles NOT into NTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake or reminder of a place or event.

clue.text: See 2
Secret police have leader of students under arrest

indicators.note: under means in this down entry the letter goes below the other piece

parts.note: the Stasi was the East German secret police

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of students

explanation.surface: Secret police take the ringleader of protesting students into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrest' looks like the police's action but is a noun meaning a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrest as a noun means a stopping, a state of no change or motion.

clue.text: Shiny stuff brought round in outrigger canoes

indicators.note: brought round means the letters found are turned to read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words outrigger canoes

explanation.surface: Glossy material has been carried along in boats with floats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into outrigger canoes, where ERCAN sits; 'brought round' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl is an iridescent lustrous substance lining shells.

clue.text: Chaplin film in Greenland?

explanation.surface: A Charlie Chaplin movie is set in the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: Limelight (1952) starred Chaplin; a land lit in lime-green would be a 'lime light' land.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaplin's 1952 movie title; also, whimsically, a green glow, lime being a green colour.

clue.text: Large girl with proposition for mathematician

parts.note: Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A big girl with a proposal for a maths expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A subsidiary theorem proved as a step toward a larger result.

clue.text: See 10
No seamen arranged flowers

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of no seamen are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors are not doing the flower arranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Windflowers are a genus of plants in the buttercup family.

clue.text: Close to border, say, in a Canadian city

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of border is taken

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Near the frontier, as it were, lies a town in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to border' reads as 'near the frontier' but means its last letter, R.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Saskatchewan is a city in Canada's prairies.

clue.text: Treacle for Missouri girls

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for Missouri
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Sweet syrup for young women from Missouri.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick dark syrup from sugar refining, British treacle being much the same.
